pointers.sentence: `{% partialdef ship_row %}` … `{% endpartialdef %}` defines one, which renders nothing where it stands unless the tag adds `"inline"`; `{% partial ship_row %}` renders it with the context at that point; and a name such as `"fleet/port_detail.html#ship_row"`, given to `Engine.get_template` and so to `render_to_string` and `{% include %}`, loads the fragment alone, a `PartialTemplate` (`django/template/defaulttags.py:partialdef_func`, `django/template/engine.py:Engine.get_template`).

The store they rely on came in 5.1: `Parser.extra_data`, a dictionary a compile function may fill, which `Template.compile_nodelist` keeps as `Template.extra_data` once the parse succeeds; `{% partialdef %}` files each fragment there under `"partials"` (`django/template/base.py:Template.compile_nodelist`).
In `{{ port..name }}` the lookup's middle part is an empty name, tried as a key, an attribute and an index like any other (`django/template/base.py:Variable._resolve_lookup`).

`Library.simple_block_tag` (5.2) makes a tag with a body from a function: the compile function parses up to the end tag, and at each render the body, rendered in the same context, is passed as the function's `"content"` argument (`django/template/library.py:Library.simple_block_tag`, `django/template/library.py:SimpleBlockNode.get_resolved_arguments`).

`{% querystring %}`, new in 5.1, writes a link's query string from the request's and the template's values, so that a link to the next page keeps the rest of the query (`django/template/defaulttags.py:querystring`).

[The built-in tags](../templates/tags.md) has the tag, and `{{ forloop.length }}` (6.0), the sequence's length, which `ForNode.render` sets before the first item (`django/template/defaulttags.py:ForNode.render`).

A callable a variable's lookup finds is not called if it carries a true `"alters_data"`: the value becomes the engine's `"string_if_invalid"`, unless a true `"do_not_call_in_templates"`, tested first, keeps the callable itself (`django/template/base.py:Variable._resolve_lookup`).

In 5.2 the flag was set on `QuerySet.create`, `QuerySet.bulk_create`, `QuerySet.get_or_create`, `QuerySet.update_or_create`, `UserManager.create_user`, `UserManager.create_superuser` and their coroutine twins, to prevent side effects when a template is rendered, say the release notes (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.create`, `django/contrib/auth/models.py:UserManager.create_user`, `docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

A manager's copy of a queryset's method carries it too, being made with `functools.wraps` (`django/db/models/manager.py:BaseManager._get_queryset_methods`): given Port's manager as ports, `{{ ports.create }}` renders the empty string, and the table stays empty.

The function `urlize`, behind the filters `|urlize` and `|urlizetrunc`, links an address that begins `"http://"` or `"https://"`, and a name with no scheme, such as `"www.harbour.org"` or one ending in one of the seven original top-level domains (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer`).

Such a name still gets `"http://"`, with a `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` since 6.0, unless the transitional setting `URLIZE_ASSUME_HTTPS` is true, which gives it `"https://"` (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.handle_word`).
Setting it raises no warning: the settings object warns for the other transitional settings, not this one (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).

The length_is filter was removed in 5.1, and a template that uses it now fails to compile with a `TemplateSyntaxError` that says `"Invalid filter: 'length_is'"` (`django/template/base.py:Parser.find_filter`, [The built-in filters](../templates/filters.md)).
